verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: Table 0 (sheet 'Report', data rows 5–16 under header row 4) is the only detected table; merged title rows A1:D1 and A2:D2 and the A4:B4 / C4:D4 header band are decorative, not data.

Target schema is closed (additionalProperties false) with exactly sku, product_name, price, currency, qty, and table 0 supplies four of them; the fifth pointer /currency has no matching source column, so it must be resolved as a single workbook-level constant (ISO 4217 code supported by the source) rather than a per-row mapping.
SKU values display as zero-padded strings ('000001'…) while the profiled type is int; the /sku mapping must cast to string (not strip_leading_zeros) to satisfy 'preserve leading zeros'.
No TOTAL row was detected inside the table range (all 12 rows carry distinct SKUs), but per the operator requirement any trailing TOTAL row must be excluded rather than mapped as a product.

Selling price carries no currency symbol, VAT flag or unit-of-measure column, so no VAT adjustment, unit conversion or currency inference is justified from this file alone; the price is taken at face value as the requested selling price.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Report' carries a title row 'Inventory and price list' followed by a single flat, one-row-per-item list of 12 unique product records with SKU, product name, selling price and stock pieces — i.e. the master product population the contract asks to preserve, not a promotion, category or standalone price list. It does contain a stock column, but the row grain is the product identity (SKU unique, one name per SKU), so 'products' is the primary role.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU' matches identity.sku; 12 distinct values in 12 rows (unique_ratio 1.0) — the natural key. Values appear zero-padded ('000001'…'000012') in top_values even though the column reads as int, so it must be cast to string to preserve leading zeros as the contract requires.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name' maps directly to product.name; 12 distinct non-null values, one per SKU row, so it is the descriptive master name rather than a category or variant label.

columns.name: Selling price
columns.reason: Header 'Selling price' states a selling (not cost) amount, matching price.amount 'Requested selling price, not cost'. Values are non-null for all 12 rows and rise monotonically 67→254, consistent with a per-item price rather than a total; no currency symbol appears in the column, so currency must come from workbook context.

columns.name: Stock pieces
columns.reason: Header 'Stock pieces' explicitly states the unit as individual pieces, matching stock.qty 'Stock in individual pieces'; non-null for all 12 rows with no TOTAL value, and no separate unit column means no unit_normalize step is needed.

changes_from_draft: Currency corrected: the draft defaulted to THB, but workbook cell A2 states 'Currency: EUR', so /currency is now the constant EUR (confidence raised to 0.95).
Added the missing /qty mapping from 'Stock pieces' (was listed as unmatched): the header and the A2 note both state the quantity is in individual pieces, matching stock.qty with no unit conversion.

/sku now casts to string after whitespace normalisation so the zero-padded text values '000001'..'000012' are preserved as required; no zero-padding operation is added because the cells already store the zeros as text.
Added a record filter excluding the 'TOTAL' summary row (A18, price 1926 / stock 234) in addition to the table's drop_total_rows, and set dedupe on /sku with keep=first.
/sku uniqueness downgraded from warning to error since SKU is the contract identity key and is unique across the 12 real rows.
No VAT, unit or currency inference was made beyond what cell A2 states explicitly; no per-row currency symbol or VAT column exists.
